title: Common thinking traps (cognitive biases)
trouble: Rereading feels like knowing; it is not. Recall, then check.

blocks.html: Everyone's mind takes shortcuts, and most of the time they serve us well. These twelve are the places where the shortcuts lead us wrong in predictable ways. Knowing their names makes them easier to catch, in yourself first.

How to hold it: Encode each bias with your own example: after reading the everyday one, think of a time it happened to you and say it out loud. A personal story is far stickier than a definition. Chunk them by what they bend (judging numbers, looking ahead and back, beliefs and choices, judging people). Then practice retrieval in real life: name a bias when you see it in an ad or a story.
This list has 12 items. Answer below, then check — the practice button generates fresh questions from the list itself.
